title: SAGE substrate: fix node-operator key path (infra blocker)
description: Infra fault outside this repo, blocking ticket jl2.3 (SAGE token mint). Container sage-substrate-sage-1 cannot issue new MCP tokens: HTTP 503 'node operator identity unavailable'. Root cause: SAGE_AGENT_KEY unset in container env -> service reads /root/.sage (directory) as the key file -> 'HTTP MCP: cannot load agent key — transport disabled'. FIX: add env SAGE_AGENT_KEY=/root/.sage/agent.key to the sage service in /Users/s-a-c/infra/sage-substrate/docker-compose.yml, then docker compose up -d --force-recreate sage. Verify: docker exec -e SAGE_AGENT_KEY=/root/.sage/agent.key sage-substrate-sage-1 sage-gui mcp-token create --name samples-20260717-probe returns a token, then revoke it. Affects every project needing new tokens (samples-20260717, chinook rotations). Owner: infra/sage-substrate.
close_reason: Fixed: data/config.yaml had agent_key_file: '' (empty string overrode the env var, making the service read /root/.sage as a file). Set agent_key_file: /root/.sage/agent.key in /Users/s-a-c/infra/sage-substrate/data/config.yaml; also added SAGE_AGENT_KEY env to both sage + sage-mcp-proxy services in docker-compose.yml as defense-in-depth. Restarted sage container. Verified: log shows 'node operator key registered' (INFO); probe token minted + revoked; real samples-20260717 token minted (id 80e9e94d-e142-414e-8b0b-ff0f0820cd04). Note: infra compose + config.yaml changes are in the substrate repo, not committed here.

title: samples-20260717 workspace bootstrap
description:
# Wayfinder Map — samples-20260717 workspace bootstrap

## Destination

A fully wired project workspace on `samples-20260717` where: **bd** holds tasks/issues, **Infisical** holds secrets (single source of truth), **SAGE** holds governed agent memory (`project/samples-20260717`), **Siyuan** holds project PKM (full integration), **AGENTS.md** routes to global `~/.config/agents/AGENTS.md`, and **~/docs/** records the integration (full parity). All scoped per-host via direnv, fail-closed, mirroring the chinook-laravel pattern where one exists.

## Notes

- **Skills every session consults:** `sage-home`, `sage-usage`, `beads`, `wayfinder`.
- **Reference impl:** `~/Herd/chinook-laravel` for beads/SAGE/AGENTS.md; **none** for Siyuan (first-of-kind → research ticket).
- **Tracker:** bd (beads) — overrides the global GitHub Issues default for this repo.
- **Standing preferences:** Infisical as source of truth, `.env.sage` as cache; 1 shared SAGE token; all 7 hosts; fail-closed on missing identity.
- **Playbooks:** `docs/20-operations/2005-memory/200502-project-integration-guide.md` (generic), `200517-chinook-laravel-integration-example.md` (worked example).

## Decisions so far

- Namespace `project/samples-20260717` (matches repo dir).
- SAGE token model: **1 shared bearer** across all hosts (single-operator trade-off: lose per-host revocation, gain one secret).
- Secret store: **Infisical** (not hand-written `.env.sage`); `.env.sage` is hydrated cache + offline fallback.
- Hosts: **all 7** — OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Zed, Junie, GitHub Copilot.
- Env-var layering: 4 export names cover 7 hosts — `SAGE_OPENCODE_*`, `SAGE_CODEX_*`, `SAGE_CLAUDE_*`, unprefixed `SAGE_MCP_*` (Cursor/Zed/Junie/Copilot).
- Siyuan: full integration; research ticket decides the how.
- docs: full parity (index registration + worked-example + project `docs/agents/`).

## Not yet specified

- Siyuan isolation/token model (per-notebook token vs global token + ACL) — graduates after the Siyuan research ticket.
- Siyuan agent access path (MCP server vs direct HTTP) — graduates after the Siyuan research ticket.
- Beads Dolt sync behaviour over the GitHub remote — resolves during the beads bootstrap ticket.

## Out of scope

- `sage-pgaak` server project-scoping (separate identity/persona).
- Spoke Worker Memory / Hub & Spoke registration.
- Editing any host's **global** config (`~/.opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`).
- Storing task state in SAGE (bd owns that).
- Infisical workspace-level secret changes (project-scoped only).
- Tier-2 hosts whose HTTP-MCP support is unconfirmed — document + revert if unsupported.
